The second objective, reading and representing information in pictograms using vertical/horizontal arrangements, is the foundational skill of interpreting and constructing pictograms. The first objective, mentioning the usefulness of a pictogram including finding the mode, depends on being able to read/interpret the pictogram first, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. Same-rank direction is justified by this substantive skill dependency (interpret/construct precedes interpreting significance/mode), not merely shared hierarchy or word overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under Topic '2. Length'. The first objective ('measure length and distance in their natural units', objective 4) develops the core measuring skill, while the second ('apply the length and ordering of lengths in our environment', objective 5) applies and extends length concepts to real-world objects and ordering. Proficiency in measuring length substantively supports success in applying and ordering lengths, and the source sequence (4 then 5) within the same topic reinforces this developmental direction. Same-rank direction is justified by the measure-then-apply pedagogical progression rather than mere shared hierarchy or overlapping wording.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY TWO Performance Objectives under the same Subtraction topic (same-rank, rank_gap 0). The first is a computational skill ('subtract 2-digit numbers with exchanging and renaming'); the second is an application objective ('apply addition and subtraction in everyday activities'), whose LCs explicitly include 'apply subtraction in everyday activities.' Proficiency in the concrete subtraction procedure substantively supports success in applying subtraction to everyday problem contexts, and the objective numbering (2 then 3) within the same row reflects computation preceding application. This supports a directional buildsTowards from the computational skill to the applied objective rather than mere co-topic overlap. The shared 'subtraction' token, hierarchy, page, and rank proximity are corroborating but not by themselves decisive.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three (rank 2) Performance Objectives under the same Theme/Sub-Theme (Basic Operations). The first objective—distinguishing between factors and multiples (Division topic)—is conceptually coherent with the second—multiplying a 2-digit by a 1-digit number (Multiplication topic), since factors and multiples are grounded in multiplicative relationships. judgment.rationale: First (PRIMARY TWO, rank 1) objective is to collect data and arrange them in groups; second (PRIMARY THREE, rank 2) objective is to mention the usefulness of a pictogram (finding the mode). Both sit within the same Theme (Every Day Statistics) and Sub-Theme (Data Collection and Presentation), with the second's topic (Pictograms) being a data-presentation extension. Collecting and grouping data is a foundational data-handling skill that supports interpreting grouped data displayed in pictograms and identifying the mode; the lower-to-higher grade rank supports first_to_second. The connection is genuine data-handling coherence rather than mere shared wording (only generic tokens like 'data', 'of' overlap), so a developmental direction is warranted but modest.
